name: DGN-410 / 460 / 520 Canister Filter
summary: A 24 V canister with a brushless DC pump, so you can wind the flow up or down instead of choking it with a tap. All three sizes share the same pump and footprint; the bigger numbers just add height and media space. The plain versions carry a 3 W UV lamp, the A versions leave it out.
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks where you want to tune flow to the scape without swapping filters.
highlights: Variable pump: 300 to 1,610 L/h at 4 to 30 W
Runs off an external 24 V adaptor
Same 24 x 24 cm footprint across all three sizes
3 W UV lamp on non-A models

specs.Variants: Standard (with 3 W UV) or A (no UV)

watchOut: The flow figure is shared across the range, so the larger bodies buy you media volume rather than extra flow.

name: DGN-80 / 120 UVC Canister Filter
summary: A newer, white-bodied canister with a UVC lamp built in and a one-button prime. It comes in two sizes, each offered with or without the A suffix. Handy if green water has been a recurring headache, though a planted tank with good balance rarely needs UV running all the time.
bestFor: Medium to large community tanks where the owner wants mechanical, biological and UV treatment in one box.
highlights: Built-in UVC lamp with its own on/off switch
One-button air purge and siphon start
Clamp-lock lid and hidden carry handle
watchOut: Power draw is high for the flow (35 W and 55 W including the UV), and Boyu does not publish a recommended tank size.

name: EF / EFU Canister Filter
summary: A no-frills external canister in six sizes, with shut-off valves built into the in and out ports so you can disconnect it for cleaning without draining hoses. The EFU versions are the same bodies with a 5 W UV lamp added. Flow ratings are modest, so treat the maker's tank ranges as generous.
bestFor: Budget-minded keepers with 100 to 650 litre tanks who want canister filtration and optional UV.
highlights: Integrated shut-off valves on the head
EFU models add a 5 W UV lamp

specs.Valves: Built-in taps on inlet and outlet

watchOut: The rated tank ranges are optimistic for a planted tank; size up if you want strong circulation.

name: FEF-230 / 280 Canister Filter
summary: A squarer canister with a built-in UV steriliser on its own switch and a valve block on the head for easy disconnection. Two sizes, each in two finishes. Flow is healthy for the power it uses.
bestFor: Medium tanks around 150 to 300 litres where a budget UV canister makes sense.
highlights: Built-in UV with a separate switch
Valve block on the lid for quick disconnection
watchOut: Boyu does not state the UV wattage or a recommended tank size.

name: SP-C / SP-B Internal Filter
summary: A submersible pump head sitting on one or two slotted sponge cartridges, which makes a simple internal filter that also aerates through a venturi. It is the classic cheap internal: effective at mechanical cleaning, easy to rinse, but bulky in a small scape.
bestFor: Quarantine, hospital or grow-out tanks, and simple community tanks that need an easy internal filter.
highlights: Pump plus one or two sponge cylinders
Venturi air intake for extra oxygen
watchOut: It is large and very visible in the tank, and the maker lists the SP-2300B with the same 8 W and 300 L/h as the small model, which looks like a sheet error.

name: WF Waterfall Hang-on Filter
summary: A simple hang-on-back filter that returns water as a wide waterfall, which keeps the surface moving and breaks up oily film. There are five sizes, from a tiny 150 L/h unit up to 720 L/h. Cheap and easy to service, but the splash does drive off CO2.
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech tanks and shrimp or betta setups on a budget.
highlights: Layered media basket in the hang-on box
Surface skimming built in on the larger WF-2035 to 2055
watchOut: The waterfall return gases off CO2, so it is not ideal on an injected tank, and Boyu gives no recommended tank sizes.

name: 950F Series Internal Filter
summary: A powerhead sitting on top of a slotted strainer tube packed with sponge. The bigger 970F and 980F push a lot of water for an internal filter.
bestFor: A larger tank that needs strong extra circulation plus some mechanical filtration.
watchOut: The larger sizes are bulky and strong for a planted tank; they can flatten stem plants and are hard to hide.

name: A Series Hanging Filter
summary: A chunky hang-on-back filter with adjustable flow, an extendable intake and a media-change reminder dial. It comes either with an open media box (sponge, carbon, bio balls) or a carbon cartridge.
bestFor: A 40 to 100 litre tank where you want a simple hang-on filter you can fill with your own media.
highlights: Choice of open media box or carbon cartridge version

specs.Versions: Media box (sponge, carbon, bio balls) or carbon cartridge

watchOut: Get the media box version for a planted tank, so you can skip carbon; like all hang-on filters the waterfall return drives off some CO2.

name: C Series Canister Filter
summary: A tall, square brown canister line from C-500 to C-1600 with a push-button primer and double valve taps. The number of media baskets grows from two to five as you go up the range.
bestFor: A 100 to 190 litre planted tank on a budget where you want room for plenty of your own media.
highlights: Push-button primer and double shut-off taps
Spray bar and intake strainer included

specs.Media supplied: Carbon, quartz rings, black sponge, white wool (varies by size)

watchOut: The flow ratings are for the bare pump; packed with media and hoses the real flow is well below that, though still generous for the listed tank sizes.

name: CF Series UV Canister Filter
summary: A grey canister range from a 410 L/h mini up to the big 3000 L/h C2400, with most sizes offered with an internal UV lamp. The mid sizes share their ratings with the CF688 range in a different body.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a cheap canister with optional UV, from a 40 litre shrimp tank (CF300) to a large display (C2400).
highlights: UV lamp of 5 to 9 W on UV versions
CF300 mini canister for small tanks

specs.UV: Optional on CF600 to C2400 (UV suffix models); CF300 has no UV

watchOut: UV does nothing for algae growing on plants and can reduce some chelated trace elements if left on all the time; the C2400 is a big unit that needs cabinet space.

name: CF11008 Series CO2 Canister Filter
summary: A squared-off canister with two planted-tank extras built in: a CO2 inlet that mixes gas from your cylinder into the filter flow, and a bay that holds a standard glass heater inside the head. Three sizes rated 950 to 1450 L/h.
bestFor: A budget planted tank of roughly 60 to 140 litres where you want CO2 and heating hidden inside the filter.
highlights: CO2 inlet and mixing chamber in the filter, cylinder not included
Internal bay for a 22 to 24 mm heater keeps the tank clear of kit

specs.CO2: Built-in inlet and mixing system; connect your own cylinder and regulator
specs.Heater bay: Takes a 22 to 24 mm diameter heater (not included)

watchOut: The maker warns to turn the CO2 off before unplugging, or water can back up out of the CO2 tube; as with any filter-mixed CO2, some gas can collect in the canister.

name: CF2000 Pre-Canister Filter
summary: A small canister that sits in the intake line before your main filter and catches the muck first. It has its own media holder and a drain valve, so you empty the pre-filter often and open the main canister far less.
bestFor: A planted tank with lots of leaf litter or trimmings where you are tired of stripping down the main canister.
highlights: Traps debris before it reaches the main canister

specs.Pump: None, runs on your main canister's flow

watchOut: It has no pump of its own, adds another hose run and some flow resistance, and must be kept clean or it will choke the main filter's flow.

name: CF688 Series Canister Filter
summary: A round blue canister range from 800 to 1400 L/h, each size available with or without a built-in UV lamp (the UV versions add a UV suffix). The UV sits inside the canister behind a safety switch.
bestFor: A 60 to 140 litre tank that suffers green water now and then, where a UV option in the same box saves buying a separate unit.
highlights: Optional internal UV lamp of 5 to 9 W
Spray bar, lily-style inlet/outlet pipes and directional spout included

specs.UV: Optional; UV models are CF688UV, CF888UV, CF1288UV, CF1488UV (uvW applies to these)

watchOut: UV only kills free-floating algae and microbes, not algae on leaves, and running it constantly can break down some chelated trace elements, so many planted-tank keepers only switch it on when needed.

name: F Series Internal Filter
summary: A tall, slim internal filter in three sizes with a blue flow-adjust knob on top; the small F-800 can take a rain bar.
bestFor: A mid-sized tank where you want an internal filter that tucks into a back corner.
watchOut: Like any internal box it takes up room in the scape and holds less media than a canister.

name: FB Internal Filter
summary: A plain rectangular internal filter with a sponge body and a side outlet that can take a rain bar. Four sizes cover roughly 50 to 140 litres.
bestFor: A basic community or planted tank where a simple sponge internal filter is enough.
highlights: Rain bar option for spread flow
watchOut: Media volume is small, so it needs rinsing often in a heavily stocked tank.

name: FC Filter Box
summary: Slim box-shaped internal filters with the pump at the bottom and a waterfall-style outlet at the top. Most use a drop-in sponge and carbon cartridge, and the range runs from tiny nano sizes up to the tall FC-601.
bestFor: A small desktop or nano tank that needs a compact, cheap internal filter.
highlights: Low-mounted pump pulls from near the substrate
Drop-in cartridge, so no wet hands

specs.Media: Sponge and carbon cartridge (FC-601 uses layered media)

watchOut: Cartridges are an ongoing cost, and the waterfall outlet splashes, which is poor for CO2; for planted tanks swap the carbon for plain sponge once it is spent.

name: H Series Hanging Filter
summary: A classic smoked-grey hang-on-back range from the tiny H-80 to the 1000 L/h H-800. Each uses a bio cartridge plus a carbon cartridge that needs changing periodically.
bestFor: A beginner tank from 25 to 200 litres where a familiar, easy hang-on filter is enough.
watchOut: The carbon cartridge is a running cost and strips some liquid fertiliser, so planted-tank keepers often swap it for sponge.

name: KF Internal Filter
summary: Very small internal filters, only 8 to 9.5 cm tall, with an adjustable outlet nozzle. The KF-160 is the slimmest of the four.
bestFor: A nano or shrimp tank of 30 to 70 litres that needs a tiny, cheap internal filter.
watchOut: The intake is not shrimp-safe as supplied, so cover it with a sponge in a breeding tank.

name: Power Head Top Filter
summary: A long plastic filter tray that sits across the top of the tank, fed by a submersible powerhead. Four lengths fit tanks from about 47 cm up to 127 cm.
bestFor: An older-style framed tank without a lid where you want a lot of cheap, easy-to-clean media.
highlights: Tray lengths to suit 47 to 127 cm tanks
watchOut: A top filter blocks part of the tank top, clashing with most planted-tank lights, and its trickle return drives off CO2.

name: SH Slim Hanging Filter
summary: A slim hang-on-back filter only 5 cm deep, with the motor down on the intake tube and a floating surface skimmer built into the intake. Sizes differ mainly in how many standard carbon cartridges they hold.
bestFor: A 20 to 80 litre tank with a lid-free top where you want surface film gone without a separate skimmer.
highlights: Only 5 cm deep behind the tank
Built-in floating surface skimmer clears surface film

specs.Cartridges: One standard size across the range

watchOut: The cartridges contain carbon, which you may prefer to replace with sponge in a fertilised planted tank, and the spill-over outlet gasses off some CO2.

name: TF Internal Filter
summary: A tall corner-style internal filter that comes with a spray bar, so the return can be spread along the back of the tank instead of blasting one spot.
bestFor: A 50 to 150 litre tank where you want gentle, spread-out flow without a canister.
highlights: Slim profile for the back corner
watchOut: Internal filters take up visible space in the scape, and the media capacity is small next to a canister.

name: aqua Corner Filter
summary: The aqua is a slim internal filter shaped to sit in a back corner, which leaves more open space for the scape. Filter modules clip together, so you can add another cartridge later if you need more capacity, and there is a small media box for carbon or bio media.
bestFor: Beginner planted tanks of roughly 100 to 200 litres where you want something simple that hides in a corner.
highlights: Corner shape keeps it out of the way of your layout
Clip-in modules, expandable with extra cartridges
Media box takes carbon, SUBSTRATpro or similar
Adjustable output and a diffuser included

specs.Includes: Foam cartridges, 20 g carbon, diffuser and hose

watchOut: The listing does not give a flow figure, so on a CO2 tank you may want a separate circulation pump to be safe.

name: Aquaball
summary: The Aquaball is an internal filter with a ball-joint pump head, so you can point the outflow wherever you want surface movement. Foam cartridges handle mechanical and biological filtration, and there is a venturi if you want to add air.
bestFor: Small to medium low-tech planted tanks, or as a backup filter and circulation boost on a bigger tank.
highlights: Swivelling ball head for aiming the outflow
Adjustable flow, 480 to 650 L/h at the top end
Modular baskets, one to three depending on size
Venturi diffuser for extra oxygen when you need it
watchOut: Switch the venturi off on a CO2 tank, as the bubbles will drive off the gas you are paying for.

name: Biopower
summary: Biopower takes the Aquaball pump head and adds closed baskets filled with SUBSTRATpro, so it behaves more like a small canister hung inside the tank. It comes with a spray bar and a venturi, and the flow is adjustable.
bestFor: Medium planted tanks without room for a canister, or tanks with a heavier fish load that need more biology than a basic internal.
highlights: Closed baskets of SUBSTRATpro for more biological capacity than a sponge filter
Spray bar included for gentle surface movement
watchOut: It is a tall column inside the tank, so plan your hardscape to hide it.

name: Classic
summary: The Classic is the round green canister that has been running on aquariums for decades. It is one open chamber you fill with whatever media you like, with no prefilter tray, electronics or clever valves to go wrong. Simple, quiet and very hard to kill.
bestFor: Keepers who want a no-fuss, long-lived canister for a planted tank and are happy to do a slightly messier clean now and then.
highlights: Single open canister, so you choose and layer the media yourself
Low running costs: 8 to 20 W depending on size
Very few moving parts, so long-term reliability is its strong point
Spare parts and replacement pads are easy to find almost anywhere

specs.Media: Supplied with pads or loose media depending on pack

watchOut: Priming is manual on the basic version and there is no quick-release tap block, so cleaning takes more effort than on newer Eheim lines.

name: classicVARIO+e
summary: This is the old Classic canister rebuilt with a brushless, WiFi-controlled pump. You set the flow from a browser, and it can ramp down at night or during feeding if paired with other Eheim digital kit. It is quiet and sips power.
bestFor: Planted tanks of about 50 to 250 litres where you want a silent, simple canister with adjustable flow and do not need a big media load.
highlights: Brushless DC pump, adjustable in fine steps
Manual and pulse modes, set over WiFi
Uses as little as 1.7 W at low flow
Maintenance reminder by e-mail when cleaning is due
watchOut: Flow tops out around 510 L/h, which is modest for a high-tech tank at the top of its size range.

name: Ecco Pro
summary: Ecco Pro is Eheim's compact entry canister, sized for small and mid-sized tanks. The carry handle doubles as the lever that locks the head and primes the filter, and media sits in stacked baskets, so cleaning is tidy. Power draw is very low.
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 60 to 300 litres where you want an easy canister that tucks into a small cabinet.
highlights: Built-in priming via the handle lever, no sucking on hoses
Stacked media baskets plus a small prefilter make cleaning quick
12/16 mm hoses on all three sizes, which suits slim lily pipes

specs.Media: Supplied complete with pads, SUBSTRATpro and hoses

watchOut: Flow is modest for the rated tank sizes, so on a heavily planted CO2 tank choose a size up or add a circulation pump.

name: Experience
summary: The Experience range sits between the Classic and the Professionel. You get a square canister with media baskets and a double-tap hose block with a single release lever, so you can close both valves and lift the filter out without spilling.
bestFor: Mid-sized planted tanks where you want easier maintenance than a Classic without paying Professionel money.
highlights: Square canister is stable and packs neatly into a cabinet
Two adjustable shut-off valves on a quick-release adaptor
Supplied with mechanical and biological media, ready to run
350 model steps up to 16/22 mm hoses and over 1,000 L/h

specs.Taps: Double tap adaptor with release lever

watchOut: The 150 and 250 are fairly gentle on flow, so on a high-tech tank you may want the next size up.

name: miniFLAT
summary: The miniFLAT lies flat on the bottom rather than hanging on the glass, so it works in very shallow water. It draws water in from underneath, passes it through a sponge and pushes it out of the top, which keeps a small water area moving.
bestFor: Very shallow nano tanks and low water levels that still need a bit of filtration and movement.
highlights: Works in water only a few centimetres deep
Sticks to the floor with suction cups
Hose connection lets you aim the outflow, for example into a small stream
watchOut: It is a tiny sponge filter, so it will not keep up with a stocked aquarium on its own.

name: Pick-up
summary: Pick-up filters are small sponge internals that stick to the glass with suckers. The motor stays put while the sponge housing slides off for rinsing, so you do not have to unclip the whole thing or wrestle the cable.
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, quarantine or shrimp tanks where a canister would be overkill.
highlights: Filter body slides off the motor for cleaning
Carbon sponge available if you want it
watchOut: Media volume is tiny, so biological capacity is limited and the sponge needs rinsing often on a well-fed tank.

name: Professionel 3 1200XL
summary: The 1200XL (type 2080) is Eheim's big canister for very large tanks. It holds 12 litres of media plus a 1.5 litre prefilter, has two intake connections and one outlet, and rolls on built-in wheels because it is heavy once full.
bestFor: Very large planted displays, roughly 600 litres and up, where one filter needs to carry a lot of media.
highlights: 12 L of media plus a large 1.5 L prefilter
Two inlet connections and one outlet, all 16/22 mm
Flow and maintenance indicator on the head
Wheels and recessed handles for moving it around
watchOut: Media is not included, it draws 45 W and is over 56 cm tall, so check cabinet height before you buy.

name: Professionel 4+
summary: The Professionel 4+ is Eheim's mechanical flagship canister, with a lift-out prefilter under the head, separate media baskets and a self-priming pump. The Xtender button reroutes water past clogged fine pads so the biology keeps running until you get round to cleaning. The 250T and 350T versions add a 210 W heater inside the canister.
bestFor: Planted tanks from about 120 to 600 litres where you want solid flow, long service intervals and, if you like, no heater in the display.
highlights: Top prefilter catches debris so the main media stays cleaner for longer
Xtender button buys a few extra days when flow starts to drop
Thermo versions (250T, 350T) hide a 210 W heater in the filter, freshwater only
16/22 mm hoses on every model, with a safety tap adaptor
Quiet ceramic shaft and adjustable flow

specs.Water type: Freshwater and marine (thermo models freshwater only)
specs.Media: Supplied complete with Eheim media and fittings

watchOut: It is a tall, fairly heavy canister, so measure your cabinet, and the thermo models are not for marine use.

name: Professionel 5e
summary: The 5e is the electronic version of the Professionel, with a brushless pump you set up over WiFi from a browser. It can hold a constant flow as the media clogs, run a pulse mode, or drop to a quieter night flow. The 600T adds a built-in 210 W heater for freshwater tanks.
bestFor: Larger high-tech planted tanks where you want strong, adjustable flow and like the idea of tuning it from your phone.
highlights: Constant-flow mode tops up pump speed as the media gets dirty
Day and night flow settings, plus pulse mode, all via WiFi in a browser
Up to 1,850 L/h with 8 L of media plus a 0.6 L prefilter on the big models
Links with Eheim's other digital kit, for example pausing flow at feeding time
600T thermo version has a 210 W heater inside, freshwater only

specs.Control: WiFi via web browser, no app needed

watchOut: It costs a lot more than the 4+, and the WiFi setup is web-based rather than a polished app, which not everyone enjoys.

name: Bioflow
summary: The large internal box filter built into Juwel aquariums, also sold on its own. Water runs down through stacked sponges and media baskets, with space for a Juwel heater inside the housing and an Eccoflow pump on top. There are no hoses, so nothing can leak outside the tank.
bestFor: Juwel owners replacing or upgrading a filter, or anyone happy with a big internal box in exchange for no hoses.
highlights: Three sizes: M (3.5 L media), L (8 L), XL (11 L)
600 or 1,000 L/h Eccoflow pump using 7 to 8 W
Room for a Juwel AquaHeat heater inside the filter
Five media stages supplied: poly pad, carbon, Nitrax, coarse and fine sponges
watchOut: It takes up a noticeable slice of the back corner and needs a tank at least 42.5 cm (M) or 60 cm (L, XL) tall.

name: BioCompact
summary: A very small internal filter for nano and quarantine tanks. It can be mounted upright or on its side, which makes it handy in shallow water, and the flow is adjustable at the outlet. The 50 has a media chamber you can refill with whatever you like.
bestFor: Nano tanks, shrimp tanks and quarantine tanks where space is tight.
highlights: Two sizes for tanks up to 25 or 50 litres
Adjustable flow of roughly 120 to 240 L/h
Can be installed horizontally for shallow water
watchOut: Tiny media capacity means frequent rinsing, and it is visible in the tank.

name: BioMaster 2
summary: Oase's main canister filter, built around a pre-filter module you lift out and rinse without opening the whole canister. Water passes through foam first, so the Hel-X biological media behind it stays clean for much longer. A heater can be retrofitted later, and there is a Thermo version with one already fitted.
bestFor: Medium to large planted tanks where you want long gaps between full cleans and easy weekly pre-filter rinses.
highlights: Five sizes for tanks from 150 to 850 litres
Pre-filter lifts out for a quick rinse without opening the canister
3 to 8 litres of media including Hel-X
Priming button and auto shut-off valves make restarts easy

specs.Pre-filter: EasyClean removable pre-filter module, 30/45 ppi sponges
specs.Safety: Automatic shut-off valve when the pre-filter is removed
specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: Rated flow drops once hoses, lily pipes and media are fitted, so size up for a heavily planted tank.

name: BioPlus
summary: A corner internal filter with a built-in, adjustable outlet nozzle instead of a separate spray bar. The media unit unclips and lifts out while the pump stays put, which makes cleaning quick. Foam plus a fine fleece stage gives decent polishing for its size.
bestFor: Small to mid-sized tanks where you want a simple internal filter that is easy to service.
highlights: Three sizes for tanks up to 50, 100 or 200 litres
Media unit lifts out for cleaning, pump stays in place
Fits neatly in a rear corner with suction cups

specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: It sits inside the tank, so it takes up scaping space and needs hiding behind plants or hardscape.

name: BioStyle
summary: A hang-on-back filter from Oase that hooks over the rim, so there are no hoses and nothing takes up space inside the tank. It uses a drop-in cartridge with foam, fleece and carbon, and a telescopic clear intake adjusts to your tank depth. Flow is generous for the size, which suits small tanks with light fish loads.
bestFor: Small planted tanks or shrimp tanks where you want easy filtration without a canister or an internal box.
highlights: Three sizes for tanks up to 70, 115 or 180 litres
Cartridge change indicator and simple swap-out media
Adjustable spacers for a secure fit on the rim

specs.Mounting: Hangs on the tank rim, adjustable spacers

watchOut: Hang-on filters splash at the surface, which drives off some CO2 in an injected tank.

name: FiltoSmart
summary: A compact, budget-friendly canister from Oase for small and mid-sized tanks. It has a self-venting start, shut-off valves on the connectors and an EasyClick lid, and it comes complete with media, hoses and pipes. The smallest model is a genuinely tiny canister that suits nano tanks.
bestFor: Nano to mid-sized planted tanks where you want a quiet canister without paying BioMaster money.
highlights: Four sizes for tanks from 60 to 300 litres
FiltoSmart 60 is small enough for a nano cabinet or beside the tank
Self-venting start-up and shut-off valves for spill-free cleaning
Flow adjustable at the inlet and outlet adapters

specs.Supplied with: Media, hoses, adapters, intake and outflow pipes, spray diffuser
specs.Thermo versions: Available with a built-in heater (models marked Thermo), which keeps the heater out of the tank

watchOut: Media volume is modest on the 60 and 100, so they need cleaning more often than bigger canisters.

name: AF-260 Top Filter
summary: A top-mounted filter box for tanks 30 to 60 cm long that sits on the rim and takes 14/16 mm hose from a pump. It gives a small tank a trickle-style media box without a sump.
bestFor: Small fish tanks where you want extra media above the water.
watchOut: Trickle boxes vent CO2, so it is not ideal for an injected planted tank.

name: CBG Hang-On Filter with UV
summary: A hang-on-back filter with an oil-film surface skimmer, double flow regulation and a built-in 5 W UV-C lamp (S models skip the UV). Two sizes for 38 to 190 litre tanks.
bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks that suffer from surface film or green water.
watchOut: UV kills free-floating algae but will not fix algae on plants or glass; the root cause still needs sorting.

name: CF Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: A simple internal filter pump in three sizes, 350 to 900 L/h. The same basic design as SunSun's HQJ pumps with a filter body.
bestFor: Small fish tanks.

name: CHJ-02 Series Internal Filter
summary: CHJ pumps fitted with a clear media column, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. Handy as a simple all-in-one internal filter.
bestFor: Small and mid fish tanks.

name: CUP-800 UV Internal Filter
summary: A compact internal filter pump with a UV-C lamp, rated for tanks from 250 to 750 litres depending on the lamp size. Flow is 700 L/h on all four models.
bestFor: Mid to large tanks with green water problems.
watchOut: Flow is modest for the tank sizes quoted, so treat it as a UV unit rather than main filtration on big tanks.

name: HBL Series Hang-On Filter
summary: SunSun's long-running hang-on-back filters, from the tiny 2 W HBL-301 up to the larger adjustable-flow HBL-800 range. They are cheap, simple and easy to service.
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, shrimp tanks and quarantine setups.
highlights: HBL-801 to 803 have adjustable flow and fit different glass thicknesses
Used in several SunSun tank kits
watchOut: Hang-on filters break the surface and can drive off CO2, and the intake needs a sponge cover in a shrimp tank.

name: HJ-42 Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ submersible pumps fitted with a sponge filter chamber, from 400 to 3,000 L/h. They can filter a tank on their own or push water through a separate filter.
bestFor: Small to large fish tanks and temporary setups.
watchOut: The bigger models make strong, noisy flow for their size; the small ones suit planted tanks better.

name: HJ-B Series Mini Internal Filter
summary: Tiny internal filters from 200 L/h, plus a few larger HJ-5x2 models up to 1,200 L/h. Several are used in SunSun's desktop tanks.
bestFor: Pico, nano and small tanks.

name: HN Internal Filter
summary: A slim 3 W internal filter for small tanks, with 300 L/h flow. Two heights.
bestFor: Nano and small tanks up to about 40 litres.

name: HQJ-I and HQJ-S Internal Filter
summary: Internal filters with a sponge column and pump head, from 300 to 500 L/h. S models add a taller filter section.
bestFor: Small fish tanks and quarantine tanks.

name: HW-300 and HW-400 Series Canister Filter
summary: The classic SunSun canisters (HW-302, 303, 304 and the 400-series equivalents), with a pre-filter tray and optional UV-C lamp on B models. They have been a common budget choice for planted tanks for years.
bestFor: Budget-conscious keepers with 100 to 500 litre planted tanks.

extra.Variants: HW-303A without UV, HW-303B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-304A without UV, HW-304B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-402A without UV, HW-402B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-403A without UV, HW-403B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C
HW-404A without UV, HW-404B with 5, 7 or 9 W UV-C

watchOut: The pumps draw more power (18 to 55 W) than newer DC canisters, and the stock hoses are fairly stiff.

name: HW-3000 Series Frequency Canister Filter
summary: SunSun's variable-speed canister, with a touch display that steps the pump through six or seven flow levels and a built-in 9 W UV-C lamp. An oil-film skimmer comes with it to clear surface scum.
bestFor: Large planted or community tanks (roughly 200 litres and up) where adjustable flow is useful.
highlights: 1,200 to 4,600 L/h depending on model and setting

specs.Control: LED touch screen for flow and UV timer

watchOut: These are big units (up to 55 cm tall and 10.5 kg on the HW-5000), so check your cabinet height first.

name: HW-500 Series Canister Filter
summary: An older SunSun canister range with rotating in/out connections, from small 320 L/h models up to the 1,000 L/h HW-507. B versions of the 504, 505 and 507 add a UV-C lamp.
bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks where you want a simple canister.
highlights: UV-C on B versions (5 or 9 W)

extra.Variants: HW-504A without UV, HW-504B with 5 W UV-C
HW-505A without UV, HW-505B with 9 W UV-C
HW-507A without UV, HW-507B with 9 W UV-C

watchOut: SunSun does not list flow or head for the HW-504 and HW-505.

name: HW-600 Series Mini Canister Filter
summary: A small canister for nano and small tanks, sold with a separate pump (B models) or as a bare filter body. Flow is 400 to 800 L/h.
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, 30 to 100 litres, that want canister filtration.
highlights: Bare versions let you use your own pump

name: HW-700 Series Canister Filter
summary: A three-size canister range from 1,000 to 2,000 L/h, each sold as an A version (no UV) or B version with a 9 W UV-C lamp. It is SunSun's current take on the popular HW-300 series.
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks, roughly 150 to 500 litres, on a budget.

extra.Variants: HW-702A without UV, HW-702B with 9 W UV-C
HW-703A without UV, HW-703B with 9 W UV-C
HW-704A without UV, HW-704B with 9 W UV-C

watchOut: Budget canisters vary in seal quality; check the lid O-ring when setting up and after cleaning.

name: JF Biochemical Sponge Filter
summary: A twin sponge filter driven by a small 3 W electric pump instead of an air pump, in three widths. It gives gentle flow and a big sponge surface for bacteria.
bestFor: Shrimp tanks, fry tanks and small planted tanks that need gentle, safe filtration.

name: JP-09 Series Internal Filter
summary: Three internal filters with a spray bar on the outlet, from 250 to 650 L/h. Low wattage (3 to 7 W).
bestFor: Small tanks where you want gentle, spread-out return flow.

name: JP-F Series Internal Filter
summary: SunSun's JP submersible pumps with tall sponge filter columns attached, from 300 to 1,600 L/h. The JP-02x/B versions are the same pumps with a short intake strainer instead.
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks.

name: JS Three-in-One Top Filter
summary: A rim-mounted top filter box with its own pump, whose support arms extend to fit different tank widths. Two sizes, 350 and 650 L/h.
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks that want easy-access top filtration.
highlights: Adjustable arms (24 to 41 cm, or 41 to 61 cm)
Filter box sold separately as JS-400B/600B
watchOut: Like any trickle filter, it drives off CO2 and splashes more than a canister.

name: JUP UV Internal Filter
summary: An internal filter with a UV-C lamp built into the body, from 500 to 800 L/h. Lamp sizes run from 5 to 13 W.
bestFor: Tanks fighting green water that want the UV inside the tank.
watchOut: UV clears green water but will not fix nutrient or light problems causing algae on plants.

name: XBA Clip-On Filter
summary: A very small 2.5 W clip-on filter with an activated carbon plate, for tanks under 40 cm. Flow is up to 300 L/h.
bestFor: Pico and nano tanks, betta setups.
watchOut: Carbon removes liquid fertiliser too, so swap it for sponge in a planted tank.

name: XBL Hang-On Filter
summary: A small hang-on filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line, in four sizes for tanks up to 30, 40, 50 and 60 cm. Flow is 300 or 500 L/h.
bestFor: Nano and small tanks under 60 cm.
highlights: Sized by tank length (30 to 60 cm)

name: XN Low Water Level Filter
summary: An internal filter built to work in shallow water, with one, two or three stacked media sections. Every size runs the same 10 W, 800 L/h pump.
bestFor: Shallow tanks and low water levels where a normal internal filter would suck air.

name: XQP-F Internal Filter
summary: The Xiaoli-line version of SunSun's filter pumps, with a filter box on the intake, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. The same pumps are sold bare as the XQP water pumps.
bestFor: Small to mid tanks.

name: XWA Series External Filter
summary: An external filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line with stacked media trays (three or five tiers) and an optional 9 W UV-C lamp. Flow runs from 500 to 1,400 L/h.
bestFor: Small to mid tanks where you want lots of media volume in a compact external box.

extra.Variants: 3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C
3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C
3 or 5 media trays; U versions add 9 W UV-C

name: Blitz Stainless Steel Filter
summary: A tiny canister filter with a brushed stainless steel body and matching steel pipes. It is made for nano tanks where a plastic canister would look out of place, and it runs quietly on low wattage.
bestFor: Nano and desktop tanks where the filter sits on show next to the aquarium.
highlights: Two sizes: 6 oz (tanks up to about 10 L) and 32 oz (up to about 45 L)
Stainless steel canister with matching inflow and outflow pipes
6 oz runs from USB; 32 oz uses a 12 V supply

specs.Included: Canister, steel inflow and outflow pipes, clear tubing, power cable, tool, foam mat

watchOut: Media capacity is small, especially on the 6 oz, so expect to clean it more often than a bigger canister.

name: Delta Canister Filter
summary: A compact white canister range that covers everything from a 5N nano to a 120 cm tank. Version 2 ships with Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes and media, it self-primes, and the baskets lift out separately for cleaning.
bestFor: Nano to mid-size planted tanks where you want a small, tidy canister with clear lily pipes out of the box.
highlights: Rated for tanks up to about 61 L, 102 L, 250 L and 348 L
Low power draw: 7 W to 24 W
Aquario Neo Flow inflow and outflow pipes included (V2)
Neo Flow add-ons (skimmer, CO2 mixer, gentle outlet) fit straight on

specs.Included: Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes, filter media (V2)

watchOut: Real flow at working height is roughly half the headline figure, so size up if you run CO2 in a densely planted tank.
